title: Bring out a piece
objective: Develop two pieces toward useful central squares.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original beginner lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Developing means bringing a piece off its starting square to do a job. White's bishop can move from f1 to c4, where it watches the centre and helps make room for castling later.
steps.detail: Both sides have moved central pawns and knights. Try one bishop move before planning the next piece.
steps.coach_prompt: Give your bishop a useful job.

question.prompt: Move your bishop from f1 to c4.
hints: Follow the clear diagonal up and left from f1.

tree.feedback: Yes. Bc4 brings out a new piece, watches the centre, and clears a path for White to castle later.
Bb5 develops well too. For this guided setup, try c4 so we can compare the next move.
Be2 is a safe developing move. Here, try the more active square c4 for this setup.

question.other_legal_move_text: That may be a useful move. For this guided setup, bring the bishop from f1 to c4.

steps.explanation: Black developed a bishop too. White still has one knight on its starting square. Bring it toward the centre, where it can support the pawn on e4.
steps.detail: A move can be useful because it improves a piece and helps another part of the position.

question.prompt: Develop your remaining knight toward the centre.
hints: Find White's knight that has not moved yet.
Move the knight from b1 to c3.

tree.feedback: Yes. Nc3 brings out the knight, supports e4, and watches the central square d5.
Na3 develops the knight, but from the edge it reaches fewer central squares. Try c3 here.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may be useful, but this exercise asks for the undeveloped knight to head toward the centre.

takeaway: Develop a new piece to a useful square. Ask what it attacks, protects, or prepares.
